0.0.n: Together with ん, this stretched-out exclamation announces a reveal or arrival.

0.1.n: This completes じゃーん; it has no separate meaning here.

0.3.n: Points out the speaker’s current location, with a slightly more polished feel than ここ.

0.4.n: This is the name of the Japanese city where HEP FIVE is located.

0.5.n: Links Osaka to HEP FIVE, identifying its location.

0.6.n: The first part of HEP FIVE, the name of a shopping complex in Osaka.

0.8.n: The second part of the shopping complex’s name, HEP FIVE.

0.9.n: Marks HEP FIVE as the destination reached.

0.10.n: The polite past form of 着く reports that the speaker has reached the destination.

1.0.n: Sets the time for the speaker’s plan.

1.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic: what the speaker plans to do today.

1.2.n: Refers to HEP FIVE, where the speaker has just arrived.

1.3.n: Marks the location where the planned activity will happen.

1.4.n: Names the attraction the speaker plans to ride.

1.5.n: With 乗る, に marks the vehicle or attraction being boarded.

1.6.n: 乗る becomes 乗りたい with たい to express the speaker’s desire.

1.7.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

1.8.n: The polite form of 思う; with たいと, it presents a wish as a gentle statement of intention.

2.0.n: A casual cheer, stretched out to show excitement.

3.0.n: Softens the speaker’s wish rather than specifying a small amount.

3.1.n: Refers to the time around dusk, before night.

3.2.n: Links 夕方 to 観覧車, describing the Ferris wheel experience at that time.

3.3.n: Refers to the same attraction the speaker mentioned earlier.

3.4.n: Marks what the speaker wants to ride, as required by 乗る.

3.5.n: The たい form of 乗る expresses the speaker’s wish.

3.6.n: Introduces the reason for the action described in the next line.

4.0.n: Pairs with から to indicate when the speaker will start moving.

4.1.n: Marks 今 as the starting time for the next action.

4.2.n: Refers to the interior of the building.

4.3.n: Marks the destination of 入る: the building’s interior.

4.4.n: The て-form of 入る connects entering with the next action.

4.5.n: Adds a friendly conversational touch while the speaker explains the next steps.

4.7.n: Combines with 乗り場 to specify which attraction’s boarding area is meant.

4.8.n: Names the place where people get onto a vehicle or ride.

4.9.n: Marks the boarding area as the endpoint of the movement.

4.10.n: Combines with します to form a verb meaning to move from one place to another.

4.11.n: An elongated します, the polite form of する; with 移動, it announces the speaker’s next movement.

5.0.n: Describes this visit as the speaker’s first.

5.1.n: The plain past form of 来る refers to the speaker’s arrival here.

5.2.n: A sentence-ending の adds a casual explanatory tone; it does not show possession here.

5.4.n: Identifies the place visited, added after the main statement in casual speech.

5.5.n: The first part of the place name HEP FIVE, added to clarify ここ.

5.7.n: Completes HEP FIVE, the name of the shopping complex.

6.0.n: Used alone as an excited reaction; the speaker leaves out the rest of the sentence.

6.2.n: A casual transition from talking about the plan to carrying it out.

6.4.n: Part of 行ってきます, a set phrase used when leaving with the expectation of returning.

6.5.n: An elongated ます completes 行ってきます, giving the farewell a cheerful sound.

0.lit: Ta-da! Here, at Osaka’s HEP FIVE, I have arrived!
0.tip: 着きました is the polite past of 着く, and に marks the destination reached.

1.lit: Today, here, I think I want to ride the Ferris wheel!
1.tip: たいと思います often announces a plan gently, rather than expressing uncertainty.

2.tip: The long vowel makes this casual cheer sound extra enthusiastic.

3.lit: Because I kind of want to ride the early-evening Ferris wheel,
3.tip: ので gives a reason and connects this unfinished line to the next action.

4.lit: From now, I’ll go inside, you know, and move to the Ferris wheel boarding area.
4.tip: 入って links entering the building to the next action, moving to the boarding area.

5.lit: For the first time I came, you see—here, HEP FIVE.
5.tip: Casual speech can add the location after the main statement, as ここHEP FIVE does here.

6.lit: Looking forward to it! Well then, I’m going and coming back!
6.tip: 行ってきます is a standard departure phrase, implying that the speaker will return.
